title: Homeostasis and Feedback
seo_title: Homeostasis Worksheets: Negative and Positive Feedback, Insulin and Glucagon (Biology)
standard_text: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that feedback mechanisms maintain homeostasis.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on homeostasis (NGSS HS-LS1-3): body temperature, blood glucose, insulin and glucagon, and negative and positive feedback. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Negative feedback reverses a change and brings it back to the set point.
body_html:
How to think about it

Change → sense → respond → back to normal.

  • Negative feedback reverses a change: too hot → sweat; too much glucose → insulin.
  • Positive feedback makes a change bigger until an event ends (childbirth, clotting).
Example

Blood glucose is 180 mg/dL. Which hormone?

Too high

Insulin lowers it

Answer: insulin

Example

Body temperature is 35.8 °C. Response?

Too low

Make heat

Answer: shivering

Common mistakes

  • Thinking insulin raises blood sugar. It lowers it.
  • Thinking shivering cools you down. It makes heat.
  • Thinking negative feedback means something bad. It means reversing a change.

faq.q: What is the difference between negative and positive feedback?
faq.a: Negative feedback reverses a change (sweating cools you). Positive feedback makes a change bigger (stronger contractions in childbirth).
When it is high, the pancreas releases insulin to lower it. When it is low, it releases glucagon to raise it.
Measure heart rate, breathing rate or body temperature before and after exercise, then record how long they take to return to normal.
